(i) most enhancer-promoter interactions are compatible, (ii) enhancer sharing is widespread among eukaryotic genomes, and (iii) enhancer distance is an important determinant in the regulation of gene neighbors.

the physical interaction between enhancer regions and promoters of target genes.
the mechanisms that underlie the spatial organization of the eukaryotic genome, and how this organization affects the regulation of genes.
the physical interactions of regulatory elements in eukaryotic cells.

enhancer sharing and EP distance are important layers of information in gene regulatory processes, which are not necessarily deterministic but rather stochastic.
the enhancer–promotor interaction is a stochastic process that is guided by physical proximity and that is influenced by the distance of the interacting partners.

enhancer sharing and enhancer–promotor distance are important factors that shape gene expression across organisms.
enhancer sharing, and the distance between enhancers and their target genes, are important layers of information in gene regulatory networks.
